core_obligations: Observe that any open V on which all H^i(E) are finite locally free is contained in U, so it remains to show that each point of U has an open neighbourhood inside U on which the cohomology is finite locally free (proof lines 12729-12735).

Replace X by an open neighbourhood of the point so that E is represented by a strictly perfect complex E^bullet concentrated in degrees [a, b], and argue by induction on b - a (proof lines 12736-12739).

Show H^b(E) is finitely presented and hence finite free on a neighbourhood of the point because its stalk is free, then arrange the direct sum decompositions E^b = Im(d^{b-1}) + H^b(E) and E^{b-1} = Ker(d^{b-1}) + Im(d^{b-1}) (proof lines 12740-12749).
Note that the truncated complex ending in Ker(d^{b-1}) is strictly perfect and perfect with the same cohomology outside degree b, then conclude by the induction hypothesis (proof lines 12750-12754).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to a strictly perfect representative on a small neighbourhood.
Induct on the length of the representative.
Split off the top cohomology and use freeness of the stalk to spread it.
Truncate and apply the induction hypothesis.
difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies the set of points where all cohomology sheaves of a perfect complex are finite free at the stalk as an open subset and shows it is the maximal open set on which all cohomology sheaves are finite locally free, assuming the local rings of the structure sheaf are local. The proof replaces X by an open neighbourhood so that E is represented by a strictly perfect complex concentrated in degrees [a, b], then runs an induction on b - a: the top cohomology is finitely presented, freeness at the stalk spreads to a neighbourhood, and a direct sum decomposition of E^b and then of E^{b-1} is arranged so that the truncated complex represents a perfect object with the same cohomology outside degree b (proof lines 12728-12754). H2: the induction on the length of a strictly perfect representative together with the two direct sum splittings is the non-routine content.
